title: `round()`: half to even by default
description: `round()` rounds half to even (`round_ties_even`): `0.5` is 0, `2.5` is 2, `-2.5` is -2. `round(mode='half_away_from_zero')` is Rust's `f64::round`, and `mode='to_zero'` truncates. `floor` and `ceil` agree with the reference on every edge case.
reference: `round` with `rounding: TIE_AWAY_FROM_ZERO` (#335), the only value the model accepts. So the writer needs `mode='half_away_from_zero'`, which matches on every row.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

`Expr.round` rounds "floating point data" with `mode` `half_to_even` (the default), `half_away_from_zero` or `to_zero`, described by value (`2.5` rounds to 2 under the default). The docstring names no float type, so it holds for `Float32` too. Settles the `Float32` row at docs level; the probes cover `Float64`.

notes: `round()` on `Float32` calls `f32::round_ties_even`, half to even as for `Float64`. With decimals it scales in `f64` and casts back.
Read at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3). The streaming engine evaluates expressions through polars-expr on each morsel (crates/polars-stream/src/expression.rs), so these kernels serve both engines.

evidence.note: `test_round_mode`, for `Float16`, `Float32` and `Float64` (lazy `collect()`): `half_to_even` gives 0.5 → 0.0, 1.5 → 2.0, 2.5 → 2.0, -0.5 → -0.0, -1.5 → -2.0, 2.25 → 2.2 and 2.75 → 2.8 at one digit; `half_away_from_zero` gives 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, -1.0, -2.0, 2.3, 2.8
`round(decimals=0, mode='half_to_even')`: half to even is the default

notes: The ties at zero digits are exact in `Float32`, so the test pins round half to even (and half away from zero by option) for `fp32` as for `fp64`.

Polars's CI runs the unit tests by default, where a lazy `collect()` without `engine` runs the streaming engine (also once with `POLARS_IDEAL_MORSEL_SIZE=4`), and again with `POLARS_ENGINE_AFFINITY=in-memory` (.github/workflows/test-python.yml#L55-L78, #L168-L178); eager `Series` and `DataFrame` calls run in memory.
